ad_intro:
Wakefit (wakefit.co, founded 2016 by Ankit Garg and Chaitanya Ramalingegowda, Bengaluru) is India's leading D2C mattress and home-furnishings brand with ~Rs.1,375 Cr FY26 annualized revenue, Q4 FY26 profit of Rs.121.7 Cr, and 201+ retail stores. We identified ~95 active creatives running across Meta in India, spending an estimated Rs.3-5 Cr/mo as management ramped A&P from 5% to 7.3-7.5% of revenue to defend against premium competition. Creative spans mattresses (61.7% of sales), furniture (30.1%), sofas, beds, wardrobes, office chairs, pillows and the new Flipper Sofa-cum-Bed.

Three obvious leaks in the funnel: (1) Offer-heavy sale creative, thin unboxing/real-room UGC - ads lead with 'Up to 65% off' sale banners and product beauty shots; customer unboxing, mattress-unrolling, room-before/after, and back-pain story Reels are thin even though home/furniture is a consideration-heavy, touch-and-feel purchase where authentic UGC drives 1.6-2.2x CVR. (2) Ad traffic lands on sale/collection pages, not SKU-direct - the running Home Upgrade Sale banner dominates and sends much paid traffic to /alloffers or category collections rather than SKU PDPs matching ad creative; mattress shoppers (high ticket, single-decision) then have to click through 3-4 layers. (3) Retargeting is sale-led instead of product-proof - browse-abandonment creative appears to be more sale reminders than mattress unboxing, warranty/sleep-trial explainers, and customer review videos at the exact moment someone is comparing 4-5 mattress brands.

Competitive heat is rising: The Sleep Company owns SmartGRID premium positioning with heavy demo-video creative, Flo has a strong lower-mid price play, and legacy Sleepwell/Duroflex are pushing D2C hard. Wakefit's IPO prospectus earmarks Rs.108 Cr for brand/marketing over 3 years - efficiency directly affects public-market narrative. We estimate 30-40% of ad spend is leaking; strong HOT lead.

findings: Creative leak: Ad mix skews heavily to studio beauty-shots and sale banners ('Up to 65% off', 'UPGRADE code ends soon'). Customer unboxing (mattress-in-a-box reveal, first-night feel), room-makeover before/after, and pain-point stories ('3 years of back pain gone') are thin. For a high-ticket (Rs.8K-25K mattress, Rs.20K-80K sofa) consideration purchase that happens once every 7-10 years, prospects need to see real customers opening, using, and keeping the product. Home/furniture UGC benchmarks show unboxing + room-makeover Reels drive 1.6-2.2x higher CVR than studio/sale creative.

Copy leak - sale fatigue: Headlines lead with 'Up to X% off' rather than sleep/furniture outcomes ('Wake up without back pain', '100-night trial - if you don't love it, we pick it up', 'Free installation in 48 hours'). Discount anchoring is particularly costly in a category where competitors (The Sleep Company, SleepyCat) compete on tech/comfort, not price. The 100-night trial and best warranty - two of Wakefit's strongest trust signals - appear as badge icons rather than headline hooks.

Landing page leak: Home Upgrade Sale banner routes significant ad traffic to /alloffers (a generic sale page) or category collections, rather than SKU-direct PDPs matched to the ad. For a mattress buyer who clicked a ShapeSense Orthopedic ad, landing on a generic sofa/wardrobe sale carousel adds friction. PDPs lead with sale price + EMI, but texture/feel close-up video, 360-degree product view, mattress-unrolling demo, and warranty/trial explainer sit below the fold. Omnichannel (nearest store, book a try) isn't surfaced in ad traffic flows.

Tracking & retargeting leak: Mattress purchase consideration is 14-45 days (couples compare 4-6 brands, test in stores, consult partners). Retargeting windows need to be longer than 7-day ecomm norms, and creative needs to layer proof at each stage (unboxing -> 30-night update -> couple testimonial -> warranty explainer -> last-call offer). Current retargeting appears sale/generic rather than SKU-specific and consideration-staged. CAPI/omnichannel attribution (201+ stores, store visits from Meta ads) appears underleveraged - a big miss for a brand with this much offline footprint.
competitors: SmartGRID patent; heavy demo-video creative (egg-drop, pressure-test); premium pricing (Rs.24-32K queen); doctor-endorsement positioning.

wins: WIN 1 - Creative: 25 Customer Unboxing + Outcome UGC Reels (14 days)

Shoot 25 vertical Reels monthly: (a) 8 mattress-in-a-box unboxing + first-unroll + first-night reaction with real couples, (b) 6 back/neck pain outcome stories (30/60/90 day updates, specific pain-type framing), (c) 5 room-makeover before/after (bed + mattress + bedside), (d) 3 sofa assembly / delivery-day vlogs (free install surprise), (e) 3 100-night-trial social-proof ("we thought we'd return it, we didn't"). Replace 35% of sale/studio creatives; pair every sale ad with a UGC variant per ad set. Add a creator-seeding program sending mattresses to 50 micro home-decor creators (50K-500K) for unscripted unboxing Reels. Expected: CTR +35-50%, CPA -20-30%. Unboxing UGC is the highest-CTR format in home/furniture.
WIN 2 - CRO: SKU-Direct Ad Landing with Sticky Trial/Warranty Bar + Nearest-Store Try (10 days)

Route 80%+ of ad traffic to SKU-direct PDPs matched to ad creative (move /alloffers routing to under 10% of spend). On top 15 SKUs (mattresses, sofas, beds): add above-the-fold sticky bar highlighting '100 Nights Trial | Free Delivery & Installation | Best Warranty | No Cost EMI'; embed a 30-second unboxing/demo video hero; add customer photo + review carousel above ATC; add a prominent 'Try at nearest Wakefit store' CTA above ATC showing 3 closest stores by pincode (drives omnichannel for 201+ stores); add a mattress-selector quiz (sleep position, weight, back pain) to route undecided shoppers. Compress hero images and lazy-load below-fold content to cut TTI by 1.5-2s. Expected: PDP CVR +25-40%, bounce rate -15-20%.
WIN 3 - Tracking: CAPI Hardening + Consideration-Staged Retargeting (14/30/60/90-day) + Omnichannel Store-Visit Ads (14 days)

Audit Meta CAPI server-side events (ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, Purchase, StoreVisit) with proper dedup against pixel. Build 5 retargeting layers matched to the long mattress consideration window: (1) 1-7 day product viewer -> unboxing video + price/EMI, (2) 7-21 day comparison shopper -> peer reviews + back-pain outcome + warranty explainer, (3) 21-45 day decider -> limited-time offer + 100-night-trial reassurance + live-chat with sleep expert, (4) cart/ATC abandoners -> free-installation reminder + countdown offer, (5) past purchasers -> protect/warranty registration + cross-sell (pillows, protectors, beds). Enable Meta Store Visit objective ads within 25km of each of 201+ stores for mattress/sofa consideration audiences. Build lookalikes from high-AOV purchasers (>Rs.30K) not just all buyers. Expected: retargeting ROAS +50-80%, omnichannel store visits +30-50%, CAC -20% within 45 days.
